newsitem.title: GERMANY: Issing says Wise Men study is a warning to Germany.
newsitem.headline: Issing says Wise Men study is a warning to Germany.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Friday a study released today predicting that Germany will not reach the deficit criteria in 1997, as outlined in the Masstricht Treaty, was to be seen as a warning.

When asked by journalists what he thought about the report, presented by the economic adviser panel known as the Five Wise Men, Issing said he had not read the study in detail and could therefore, not make any detailed comments.

He noted that the report forecast the budget deficit would be running near 3.3 percent of gross domestic product in 1997 but said that was only a prediction and not yet a fact. Nonetheless, he said the report should be taken as a warning.
"I rather see this as a warning that we need to continue to work hard," Issing said, adding "there is no question that it will be close."

Countries that wish to join a single European currency in 1999 are required to meet certain economic targets, including keeping their budget deficits below a reference value of three percent of gross domestic product.
Almost all European Union countries are facing an uphill struggle to meet this particular goal.
Issing welcomed Spain's efforts to consolidate its public finances but said that everyone knew the outcome was still not sufficient to make the single currency grade.
"One must respect the efforts, but we know, and the Spanish know too, that it is not yet enough," he said.
He said Germany similarly had not made sufficient progress.
